definition: A clear and deep understanding of something.
example: Her research provided new insight into the problem.
note: Spanish 'conocimiento' just means 'knowledge'. Changed to 'visión', which carries the idea of seeing into something.

definition: The most recent.
example: Have you seen the latest news about the city project?
note: Same word appears twice in the list; corrected the same way so the two entries agree. French and Italian said 'last' rather than 'most recent'.

definition: Not tight, or not firmly fixed in place.
example: The screw is loose and needs tightening.
note: Three of the four original translations meant 'not tight', and all had been changed to 'running free' because the example was about a dog. The first meaning of 'loose' is 'not tight'. Example and translations rebuilt around that.

definition: A way of doing or achieving something.
example: She found a means to solve the problem quickly.
note: Spanish 'significa' was the verb 'it means', which is a completely different word. Corrected to 'medio'. French was plural; made singular so all four match.

definition: To disagree with and try to stop something.
example: Many people oppose the building of the new factory.
note: Italian was missing the little linking word that Spanish and French both have. Added.

definition: An object wrapped for sending or carrying.
example: She mailed a small package to her friend.
note: Same word appears twice in the list with different Italian. Set to 'pacco' so the two entries agree.

definition: To choose one thing from several.
example: Please pick a red apple from the fruit basket.
note: French and Italian said 'to take' while Spanish and German said 'to choose'. All four now mean 'to choose', matching the definition.

definition: A marked area of ground where a sport is played.
example: The players ran onto the football pitch.
note: The four original translations all pointed at different meanings, and the entry had been settled on 'tar', which almost no learner will ever need. In British English the first meaning of 'pitch' is the sports field. Fully rebuilt around that.

definition: A secret plan to do something bad.
example: The detective uncovered the plot to steal the diamonds.
note: Same word appears twice in the list; corrected the same way so the two entries agree. Spanish and Italian 'trama' means the storyline of a book, which is a different meaning.

definition: To hold a certain position in a list or order.
example: She ranks first in her class thanks to her excellent grades.
note: Spanish was the form you use for putting other things in order, not for holding a position yourself. Changed to match the French and Italian.

definition: To put your name on an official list.
example: You can register for the class online.
note: Spanish, German and Italian all meant 'to record something', while French meant 'to sign yourself up'. All four now mean signing yourself up, which is what the example shows.

definition: To depend on someone or something.
example: I rely on my friends for good advice.
note: Spanish and Italian were missing the little linking word that German and French both have. Added.

definition: Money kept for future use.
example: She puts part of her pay into a savings account every month.
note: The example said 'a saving account'; the correct English is 'a savings account'. Italian was plural; made singular so all four match.

definition: To fasten something or make it safe.
example: Please secure the doors before you leave the house.
note: French 'verrouiller' only means 'to lock' and Italian was a three-word phrase. Both changed to single words that match the Spanish and German.

definition: To move something to a different position.
example: Please shift your car so others can park here.
note: Same word appears twice in the list with different translations. Set to the same set so the two entries agree.

definition: An event in which someone fires a gun.
example: The police investigated the shooting in the town centre.
note: Had been pushed onto a plant growing upward, which is a rare use. 'Shooting' normally means gunfire, and this now matches the entry for 'shoot'. Fully rebuilt.

definition: The firing of a gun.
example: We heard a shot in the distance.
note: Had been changed to mean an injection at the doctor's. The original German and French were both 'gunshot', which is the first meaning of 'shot'. Restored.

definition: To open something out to its full size.
example: The bird spread its wings and flew away quickly.
note: Same word appears twice in the list with different Spanish. Set to the same set so the two entries agree.

definition: To rise to an upright position on your feet.
example: Please stand when the queen enters the room.
note: Italian was not a verb at all, German 'stehen' means 'to be standing' rather than 'to get up', and Spanish 'pararse' is mainly Latin American. All four now mean rising to your feet.

definition: The topic that something is about.
example: The subject of the book was ancient history.
note: Italian 'materia' means a school subject such as maths. The word for the topic of a book is 'argomento'.

definition: To turn a device off.
example: Please switch off the lights when you leave.
note: Same word appears twice in the list; corrected the same way so the two entries agree. German 'schalten' was neutral and did not match the example.
